ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: Approximately 75:25 white-to-black pixel ratio across the visible ventral surface; high-intensity white dominates the central region with low-intensity black margins.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Large contiguous high-intensity (white) region occupying the central 75% of both lobes; continuous low-intensity (black) pigmentation along the entire trailing edge and distal tips; two distinct low-intensity circular blobs located in the upper-left quadrant of the left lobe; dark pigmentation transition at the peduncle junction.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Deep V-shaped depression with a calculated pixel angle of approximately 55 degrees and significant bounding-box depth extending toward the peduncle.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: High-frequency, variable-amplitude serrations (peaks and valleys) visible along the outer third of both trailing edges; transitioning to smoother, lower-frequency undulations near the median notch.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Strong convex curve fitted to the anterior-lateral edges of both lobes, tapering to sharp, pointed distal tips.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: High-contrast pixel clusters consistent with barnacle colonization localized on the extreme lateral tips of both the left and right lobes; additional dark spot clusters on the upper left lobe surface.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Faint vertical linear pixel disruptions (rake marks) detected on the mid-to-outer section of the right lobe near the trailing edge.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Extensive barnacle colonization on the distal tips creating irregular geometric protrusions from the natural lobe contour; multiple localized dark circular markings on the left lobe surface.
other_distinctive_markers: Two prominent, high-contrast dark circular spots in the upper left region of the white field, serving as unique spatial identifiers.
